symbols.name: n
symbols.def: The number of observations in row \(n\).

symbols.name: K
symbols.def: The number of scalar quantization cells.

symbols.name: K_n
symbols.def: The largest quantization resolution reported in row \(n\).

symbols.name: Y_{n,i}(a)
symbols.def: The potential outcome of unit \(i\) in row \(n\) under treatment \(a\).

symbols.name: P^(n)
symbols.def: The population law generating every observation in row \(n\).

symbols.name: P_X^(n)
symbols.def: The marginal law of \(X_{n,i}\) induced by \(P^{(n)}\).

symbols.name: C_{P^(n),K}
symbols.def: \(C_{P^{(n)},K}=(c_{P^{(n)},K,1},\ldots,c_{P^{(n)},K,K})\) is a minimizer over \(\mathcal C_K\) of \(C\mapsto\mathbb E_{P^{(n)}}[\min_{1\le j\le K}\{b_{P^{(n)}}(X_{n,i})-c_j\}^2]\).

symbols.name: q_{P^(n),K}
symbols.def: \(q_{P^{(n)},K}(u)=c_{P^{(n)},K,j^*(u)}\), where \(j^*(u)\) is the smallest index in \(\arg\min_{1\le j\le K}|u-c_{P^{(n)},K,j}|\).

symbols.name: H_{P^(n),K}
symbols.def: The Hessian of the population distortion with respect to the increasingly labelled centers, evaluated at \(C_{P^{(n)},K}\).

symbols.name: alpha_{P^(n),K}
symbols.def: The boundary-margin exponent at resolution \(K\) under \(P^{(n)}\).

symbols.name: M_{P^(n),K}
symbols.def: The boundary-margin coefficient at resolution \(K\) under \(P^{(n)}\).

symbols.name: kappa_{P^(n),K}
symbols.def: The radius on which the boundary-margin condition holds.

symbols.name: r_n
symbols.def: A deterministic rowwise rate controlling estimability of the propensity and outcome regressions.

symbols.name: Gamma_n(P^(n))
symbols.def: On the nondegenerate class, \[\Gamma_n(P^{(n)})=\left\{\frac{B_n(P^{(n)})^2\log^7(nK_n)}{n}\right\}^{1/6}+\max_{1\le K<K_n}\left\{\frac{\sqrt{n\log K_n}R^G_{P^{(n)},K,n}}{\sigma_{P^{(n)},K}}+\frac{\log K_n S^G_{P^{(n)},K,n}}{\sigma_{P^{(n)},K}}\right\}.\]

symbols.name: mathcal P_n^CQ
symbols.def: The class \(\mathcal P_n^{\mathrm{CQ}}\) defined in def:triangular-causal-quantizer-class.

symbols.name: hat_eta
symbols.def: The raw collection \(\widehat\eta=(\widehat e,\widehat\mu_0,\widehat\mu_1)\) fitted away from each validation fold.

symbols.name: hat_e^cl
symbols.def: For each training fold, \(\widehat e^{\mathrm{cl}}(x)=\min\{1-\epsilon/2,\max(\epsilon/2,\widehat e(x))\}\). This is an estimator construction, not a class assumption. Under ass:overlap, \(\lvert\widehat e^{\mathrm{cl}}(x)-e_{P^{(n)}}(x)\rvert\le\lvert\widehat e(x)-e_{P^{(n)}}(x)\rvert\) pointwise, so clipping preserves the foldwise \(L_2(P_X^{(n)})\) rate and uniformly bounds every inverse propensity.

symbols.name: hat_eta^cl
symbols.def: The foldwise collection \(\widehat\eta^{\mathrm{cl}}=(\widehat e^{\mathrm{cl}},\widehat\mu_0,\widehat\mu_1)\) used in every corrected loss and estimated influence score.

symbols.name: hat_C_K
symbols.def: The minimizer of the cross-fitted corrected empirical distortion at resolution \(K\), with \(\widehat e^{\mathrm{cl}}\) used in every inverse-propensity term.

symbols.name: hat_W_K
symbols.def: The cross-fitted corrected estimate \(\widehat W_K\) evaluated at \(\widehat C_K\), using \(\widehat e^{\mathrm{cl}}\) in the corrected loss.

symbols.name: hat_rho_K
symbols.def: On the event \(\widehat W_1>0\), \(\widehat\rho(K)=1-\widehat W_K/\widehat W_1\).

symbols.name: hat_sigma_K
symbols.def: The positive empirical standard deviation of the estimated cross-fitted adjacent efficient scores computed with \(\widehat e^{\mathrm{cl}}\).

symbols.name: xi_i
symbols.def: Independent Gaussian multipliers, conditionally independent of \(O_n^n\).

symbols.name: T_n
symbols.def: On the nondegenerate class and the event \(\min_{K<K_n}\widehat\sigma_K>0\), \(T_n=\max_{1\le K<K_n}|\sqrt n\{\widehat G_K-G_{P^{(n)}}(K)\}/\widehat\sigma_K|\).

symbols.name: T_n^sharp
symbols.def: On the same event, \(T_n^{\#}=\max_{1\le K<K_n}|n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\xi_i\widehat{\Delta\phi}_{i,K}/\widehat\sigma_K|\), where every estimated score uses \(\widehat e^{\mathrm{cl}}\) and is centered by \(P_{\mathrm{emp},n}\).

symbols.name: beta_W
symbols.def: The exponent in the sufficient polynomial bound for \(W_{P^{(n)}}(K)\).

symbols.name: beta_lambda
symbols.def: The exponent in the sufficient polynomial lower bound for curvature.

symbols.name: beta_s
symbols.def: The exponent in the sufficient polynomial upper bound for cell radius.

symbols.name: beta_M
symbols.def: The exponent in the sufficient polynomial upper bound for the margin coefficient.

symbols.name: beta_kappa
symbols.def: The exponent in the sufficient polynomial lower bound for the margin radius.

symbols.name: alpha_0
symbols.def: A uniform lower bound on the boundary-margin exponents.

symbols.name: beta_B
symbols.def: The exponent in the sufficient polynomial score-envelope bound.

symbols.name: beta_1
symbols.def: The exponent in \(W_{P^{(n)}}(1)\gtrsim K_n^{-\beta_1}\); the uniformly nondegenerate regime has \(\beta_1=0\).

symbols.name: beta_sigma
symbols.def: The exponent in the sufficient polynomial lower bound for \(\sigma_{P^{(n)},K}\).

symbols.name: eta_star
symbols.def: The explicit ceiling exponent derived in cor:polynomial-growth-ceiling.

symbols.name: nu_n
symbols.def: The conditional standard deviation of the efficient residual in the uniform witness.

symbols.name: P_{U,nu_n}^(n)
symbols.def: The row law with \(X_{n,i}=U\), \(A_{n,i}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) independent of \(U\), \(Y_{n,i}(1)=U-1/2+\nu_n\varepsilon_1\), and \(Y_{n,i}(0)=1/2-U+\nu_n\varepsilon_0\), where the two Rademacher marks are independent of \(U\) and treatment.

symbols.name: P_{0,K}^(n)
symbols.def: The randomized law with \(X_{n,i}=U\), \(A_{n,i}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), and conditionally independent binary potential outcomes satisfying \(P^{(n)}\{Y_{n,i}(1)=1\mid U=u\}=(u+1/2)/2\) and \(P^{(n)}\{Y_{n,i}(0)=1\mid U=u\}=(3/2-u)/2\).

symbols.name: theta
symbols.def: The scalar parameter indexing the adjacent-score transport.

symbols.name: P_{theta,K}^(n)
symbols.def: The law whose observed-data density relative to \(P_{0,K}^{(n)}\) is \(\exp\{\theta s_K^{(0)}(o)\}/\mathbb E_{P_{0,K}^{(n)}}[\exp\{\theta s_K^{(0)}(O_{n,i})\}]\), causally completed by drawing \(A_{n,i}\) from its tilted propensity and drawing \(Y_{n,i}(0),Y_{n,i}(1)\) conditionally independently from the two tilted outcome regressions.

assumptions.condition: For every row \(n\), \(Y_{n,i}=Y_{n,i}(a)\) almost surely on \(\{A_{n,i}=a\}\), for each \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
There is a fixed \(\epsilon>0\), common to all rows and laws in the class, such that \(\epsilon\le e_{P^{(n)}}(X_{n,i})\le1-\epsilon\) almost surely.
Under \(P^{(n)}\), \(\lvert\mu_{1,P^{(n)}}(X_{n,i})-\mu_{0,P^{(n)}}(X_{n,i})\rvert\le1\) almost surely; under the stated scaling this is equivalent to \(b_{P^{(n)}}(X_{n,i})\in[0,1]\) almost surely.

For every \(1\le K\le K_n\), the optimizer set of \(C\mapsto\mathbb E_{P^{(n)}}[\min_{1\le j\le K}\{b_{P^{(n)}}(X_{n,i})-c_j\}^2]\) over \(\mathcal C_K\) is the singleton \(\{C_{P^{(n)},K}\}\), and its coordinates satisfy \(0<c_{P^{(n)},K,1}<\cdots<c_{P^{(n)},K,K}<1\).

novel.justification: This proposal-specific growing-resolution condition is exactly satisfied by the uniform causal-feature witness, whose unique optimizer has centers \((2j-1)/(2K)\). It is also interpretable in applications as excluding tied population segmentations and endpoint-only cells. Pollard1982Central is a fixed-\(K\) antecedent for uniqueness, not the provenance of this uniform-in-\(K\) condition.

Allowing the smallest Hessian eigenvalue to decay with \(K\) is a growing-resolution regularity condition. It is satisfied by the uniform causal-feature witness with \(\lambda_{P^{(n)},K}=2/K\), and it permits the increasing local instability expected from progressively finer customer segmentation. Pollard1982Central supplies the fixed-\(K\) positive-Hessian antecedent only.

assumptions.condition: For every \(1\le K\le K_n\) and \(0<t\le\kappa_{P^{(n)},K}\), \[P^{(n)}\!\left\{\operatorname{dist}\!\left(b_{P^{(n)}}(X_{n,i}),B_{P^{(n)},K}\right)\le t\right\}\le M_{P^{(n)},K}\left(\frac{t}{s_{P^{(n)},K}}\right)^{\alpha_{P^{(n)},K}}.\] For \(K=1\), the left side is zero because \(B_{P^{(n)},1}=\varnothing\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(u,\varnothing)=+\infty\).

novel.justification: The arbitrary-exponent condition with \(K\)-dependent coefficient, cell-radius normalization, and validity radius is tailored to growing resolution. It is satisfied by the uniform causal-feature witness with exponent one, coefficient two, and radius \(1/(2K)\), and it allows empirical feature densities to place increasing mass near finer Voronoi boundaries. Levrard2015 is a fixed-resolution margin antecedent rather than exact provenance for this condition.

assumptions.condition: The functions \(e_{P^{(n)}}\) and \(\mu_{a,P^{(n)}}\) admit cross-fitted estimators whose maximum \(L_2(P_X^{(n)})\) error and maximum outcome-regression uniform error are \(O_{P^{(n)}}(r_n)\), uniformly over the row class.

standard.name: Cross-fitted nuisance estimability in the norm combination used for causal quantization

assumptions.condition: There is a fixed \(\underline w>0\), common to every row and law in the class, such that \(W_{P^{(n)}}(1)\ge\underline w\).

novel.justification: Because \(W_{P^{(n)}}(1)=\inf_{c\in[0,1]}\mathbb E_{P^{(n)}}[\{b_{P^{(n)}}(X_{n,i})-c\}^2]=\operatorname{Var}_{P^{(n)}}\{b_{P^{(n)}}(X_{n,i})\}\), the lower bound is the proposal-specific nonvanishing causal-heterogeneity regime needed to define and uniformly linearize the normalized ratio profile. It excludes homogeneous and drifting-to-homogeneous laws, and it is nonempty because the exact uniform witness has \(W_{P_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)}}(1)=1/12\).

standard.name: Coordinatewise variance nondegeneracy for studentized high-dimensional inference

definitions.name: The triangular causal-quantizer class \(\mathcal P_n^{\mathrm{CQ}}\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_n^{\mathrm{CQ}}=\{P^{(n)}:P^{(n)}\text{ is a population law in row }n\text{ satisfying ass:consistency, ass:exchangeability, ass:overlap, ass:bounded-feature, ass:singleton-interior-optimizer, ass:curvature, ass:margin, ass:nuisance-estimability, ass:resolution-denominator, ass:adjacent-score-nondegeneracy, and ass:score-envelope for every stated }1\le K\le K_n\}\).

definitions.name: The corrected-moment growing-resolution estimator
definitions.construction: On each validation fold, form \(\widehat e^{\mathrm{cl}}(x)=\min\{1-\epsilon/2,\max(\epsilon/2,\widehat e(x))\}\) and insert \(\widehat\eta^{\mathrm{cl}}=(\widehat e^{\mathrm{cl}},\widehat\mu_0,\widehat\mu_1)\) into the corrected loss associated with \(\phi_{W,P^{(n)},K}\). Minimize its \(P_{\mathrm{emp},n}\)-average to obtain \(\widehat C_K\), and evaluate \(\widehat W_K\) for every \(1\le K\le K_n\), always using \(\widehat e^{\mathrm{cl}}\) in inverse-propensity terms. On the event \(\widehat W_1>0\), form \(\widehat\rho(K)=1-\widehat W_K/\widehat W_1\) and \(\widehat G_K=\widehat\rho(K+1)-\widehat\rho(K)\) for \(K<K_n\).

definitions.name: The corrected-score multiplier band
definitions.construction: Compute every estimated adjacent score at \(\widehat C_K\) with \(\widehat e^{\mathrm{cl}}\), center the scores by \(P_{\mathrm{emp},n}\), compute their empirical standard deviations \(\widehat\sigma_K\), verify \(\min_{K<K_n}\widehat\sigma_K>0\), draw \(\xi_i\), evaluate \(T_n^{\#}\) from the same clipped-propensity scores, and return \(\{I_{n,K}:1\le K<K_n\}\) using \(c_{1-\alpha}^{\#}\).

definitions.name: The unresolved adjacent-resolution profile
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal A_n=\{K\in\{1,\ldots,K_n-1\}:0\in I_{n,K}\}\), accompanied by the full intervals \(I_{n,K}\).

definitions.name: The transparent polynomial regime
definitions.construction: For fixed positive constants \(c,C\), uniformly over \(P^{(n)}\in\mathcal P_n^{\mathrm{CQ}}\) and \(K\le K_n\), impose \[W_{P^{(n)}}(K)\le CK^{-\beta_W},\quad \lambda_{P^{(n)},K}\ge cK^{-\beta_\lambda},\quad s_{P^{(n)},K}\le CK^{-\beta_s},\quad M_{P^{(n)},K}\le CK^{\beta_M},\quad \kappa_{P^{(n)},K}\ge cK^{-\beta_\kappa},\] \[\alpha_{P^{(n)},K}\ge\alpha_0,\quad r_n\le Cn^{-\gamma},\quad B_n(P^{(n)})\le CK_n^{\beta_B},\quad W_{P^{(n)}}(1)\ge cK_n^{-\beta_1},\quad \sigma_{P^{(n)},K}\ge cK^{-\beta_\sigma}.\] The uniform-ratio specialization sets \(\beta_1=0\).

definitions.name: The explicit nondegenerate adjacent-score transport
definitions.construction: Start from \(P_{0,K}^{(n)}\), whose randomized propensity and binary outcome probabilities lie in \([1/4,3/4]\). For \(s_K^{(0)}=\Delta\phi_{P_{0,K}^{(n)},K}/\sigma_{P_{0,K}^{(n)},K}\), set \[\frac{dP_{\theta,K}^{(n)}}{dP_{0,K}^{(n)}}(o)=\frac{\exp\{\theta s_K^{(0)}(o)\}}{\mathbb E_{P_{0,K}^{(n)}}[\exp\{\theta s_K^{(0)}(O)\}]},\qquad |\theta|\le c_0/\|s_K^{(0)}\|_\infty.\] Complete each tilted observed law causally by its tilted propensity and its two tilted outcome regressions, with conditionally independent potential outcomes. This is a normalized, mass-preserving parametric subfamily with score \(s_K^{(0)}\) at \(\theta=0\).

definitions.name: The multi-resolution converse handle
definitions.construction: Apply a Le Cam chain or Assouad hypercube to disjoint score-aligned exponential tilts of the target object \(\{G_{P^{(n)}}(K):K<K_n\}\), then verify uniform membership by perturbation bounds for the Voronoi boundaries, curvature, margin constants, and causal nuisance radius.

statements.gap: KimKimKennedy2026 supplies a fixed-resolution influence function, but neither it nor Pollard1982Quantization computes the adjacent cancellation or its finite-\(K\) constants.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \(P^{(n)}\in\mathcal P_n^{\mathrm{CQ}}\) and every \(1\le K\le K_n\), \[\widehat W_K-W_{P^{(n)}}(K)=(P_{\mathrm{emp},n}-P^{(n)})\phi_{W,P^{(n)},K}+O_{P^{(n)}}\!\left(R_{P^{(n)},K,n}\right).\] Consequently, uniformly over \(1\le K<K_n\), \[\widehat G_K-G_{P^{(n)}}(K)=(P_{\mathrm{emp},n}-P^{(n)})\Delta\phi_{P^{(n)},K}+O_{P^{(n)}}\!\left(R^G_{P^{(n)},K,n}\right),\] and the maximum \(L_2(P^{(n)})\) discrepancy of the estimated adjacent score divided by \(\sigma_{P^{(n)},K}\) is \(O_{P^{(n)}}(\max_{K<K_n}S^G_{P^{(n)},K,n}/\sigma_{P^{(n)},K})\). The first expansion includes \(K=K_n\), so the adjacent expansion at \(K_n-1\) controls both optimized risks and the \(W_{P^{(n)}}(1)\) denominator.
statements.justification: This is the missing bridge from fixed-resolution orthogonality to a growing optimized profile with a valid ratio expansion.
statements.gap: Levrard2015 tracks fixed-level excess risk and KimKimKennedy2026 proves fixed-resolution causal expansions; neither controls both neighboring optimized risks, the common denominator, and quadratic ratio terms on the shrinking adjacent-score scale.
statements.consumer: The bound identifies whether codebook fitting, denominator estimation, or causal nuisance learning reaches the MineThatData adjacent-gain noise floor first.

statements.statement: Suppose \(K_n\to\infty\) and \[\sup_{P^{(n)}\in\mathcal P_n^{\mathrm{CQ}}}\Gamma_n(P^{(n)})\to0.\] Then the corrected-score multiplier band is uniformly valid on the same nondegenerate triangular class: \[\sup_{P^{(n)}\in\mathcal P_n^{\mathrm{CQ}}}\left|P_{P^{(n)}}\!\left\{G_{P^{(n)}}(K)\in I_{n,K}\text{ for every }1\le K<K_n\right\}-(1-\alpha)\right|\to0.\] This is a strict growing-resolution extension of the fixed-\(k\) corrected-risk machinery corroborated in KimKimKennedy2026, arXiv:2405.03083v5: Section 4.1, equation (10), and Lemma 4.1 give the fixed-\(k\) optimal-risk influence function; Section 4.2, Assumptions A4--A6, and Lemma 4.2 give root-\(n\) normality for a corrected risk at a fixed codebook; and Remark 3.1 states that \(k\) is fixed and that \(k\)-selection and increasing \(k\) are not addressed. The result here instead treats \(K_n\to\infty\), reoptimizes neighboring codebooks, studentizes possibly shrinking adjacent variances, and covers the full adjacent ratio vector simultaneously. When \(K_n=2\), it is a one-coordinate ratio delta-method specialization built from those fixed-risk scores; the normalized ratio is not itself a theorem stated by KimKimKennedy2026.
statements.justification: The theorem turns the fixed-\(k\) risk-score ingredients in KimKimKennedy2026, arXiv:2405.03083v5, Section 4.1, equation (10), and Lemma 4.1 into simultaneous inference for an entire growing causal-resolution curve.
statements.gap: KimKimKennedy2026, arXiv:2405.03083v5, Section 4.2, Assumptions A4--A6, and Lemma 4.2 establish fixed-codebook corrected-risk root-\(n\) normality, while Remark 3.1 explicitly leaves \(k\)-selection and increasing \(k\) untreated; BelloniChernozhukovChetverikovWei2018 begins from supplied score vectors. KimKimWassermanKennedy2024 instead studies plug-in hierarchical linkages and density level sets for the vector counterfactual feature, so its multiple dendrogram granularities are not coordinates of an adjacent optimized-distortion profile. None gives a band for growing reoptimized neighboring scalar squared-error \(k\)-means codebooks with shrinking adjacent variances and a common estimated ratio denominator.
statements.consumer: The band replaces visual elbow inspection by familywise-valid uncertainty for every candidate MineThatData resolution.

Fixed \(K_n\) requires only the stated nuisance thresholds. For the exact-nuisance uniform witness, the optimized-risk component instead reduces sharply to \[ rac{K_n\sqrt{\log K_n}\log(nK_n)}{\sqrt n\sqrt{1+(
u_nK_n)^2}}	o0.\] If \(
u_nK_n=O(1)\), band validity allows \(K_n=o(n^{1/2})\) up to logarithms and profile resolution additionally requires \(K_n=o(\sqrt{n/\log K_n})\). If \(

statements.justification: The corollary converts the abstract frontier gauge into an auditable ceiling and separates coverage from actual resolution.
statements.gap: Fixed-\(K\) causal quantization and generic high-dimensional bootstrap theory do not expose how curvature, distortion decay, margin radius, nuisance rate, denominator scale, and adjacent variance jointly set the maximal \(K_n\).
statements.consumer: A MineThatData analysis can plug in conservative empirical exponents and report a precommitted resolution ceiling.

statements.statement: Under thm:growing-profile-band, \(\mathcal A_n\) is locally honest. Uniformly over every triangular subfamily of \(\mathcal P_n^{\mathrm{CQ}}\) satisfying \(\max_{K<K_n}\sqrt n|G_{P^{(n)}}(K)|/\sigma_{P^{(n)},K}=O(\sqrt{\log K_n})\), the full local gain vector is covered with probability \(1-\alpha+o(1)\). Every coordinate satisfying \(\sqrt n|G_{P^{(n)}}(K)|/\sigma_{P^{(n)},K}>2c_{1-\alpha}^{\#}+o_{P^{(n)}}(1)\) is excluded from \(\mathcal A_n\) with probability tending to one. Thus unresolved resolutions are determined by standardized rather than raw adjacent gains.
statements.justification: Resolution selection is nonregular near adjacent ties, so honest inference must display ambiguity rather than force a single elbow.
statements.gap: AndrewsSoares2010 and ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2019MMI treat supplied moment systems, not moving differences of optimized causal risks.
statements.consumer: MineThatData investigators receive the resolutions that remain empirically indistinguishable together with the full familywise-valid intervals.

statements.statement: Fix a sequence \(1\le K<K_n\) for which \(\|s_K^{(0)}\|_\infty/\sqrt n\to0\), and use the explicit causal subfamily in def:explicit-adjacent-score-transport. For every fixed sufficiently small \(c>0\), let \(\theta_{n,+}=c/\sqrt n\) and \(\theta_{n,-}=-c/\sqrt n\). Then both laws remain in a common nondegenerate causal-quantizer neighborhood, \[\operatorname{KL}\!\left((P_{\theta_{n,+},K}^{(n)})^{\otimes n},(P_{\theta_{n,-},K}^{(n)})^{\otimes n}\right)\le 2c^2+o(1),\] and \[G_{P_{\theta_{n,+},K}^{(n)}}(K)-G_{P_{\theta_{n,-},K}^{(n)}}(K)=\frac{2c\,\sigma_{P_{0,K}^{(n)},K}}{\sqrt n}+o\!\left(\frac{\sigma_{P_{0,K}^{(n)},K}}{\sqrt n}\right).\] Consequently, the infimum over all tests of the sum of the two sign-classification errors is bounded away from zero. No uniformly honest procedure can force coordinate \(K\) to a resolved singleton throughout alternatives with \(\sqrt n|G_{P^{(n)}}(K)|/\sigma_{P^{(n)},K}=O(1)\). This establishes necessity only of the coordinatewise standardized-separation component; it does not claim necessity of every term in \(\Gamma_n(P^{(n)})\) or the simultaneous \(\sqrt{\log K_n}\) factor.
statements.justification: The explicit score-aligned causal experiment supplies a genuine adjacent-resolution converse without promising an unsupported full frontier.
statements.gap: Levrard2015 proves a fixed-level excess-distortion lower bound, whereas this theorem targets local discrimination of adjacent normalized causal risks in a nondegenerate randomized causal subfamily.
statements.consumer: The lower bound prevents MineThatData analysts from interpreting an unresolved standardized adjacent gain as a failure of the particular bootstrap algorithm.

statements.statement: Using def:frontier-converse-handle, determine which components of the uniform condition \(\sup_{P^{(n)}\in\mathcal P_n^{\mathrm{CQ}}}\Gamma_n(P^{(n)})\to0\) are necessary up to logarithmic factors for simultaneous coverage. On separated triangular subclasses, determine whether uniform divergence of \(\sqrt n\,d_n(P^{(n)})/\sqrt{\log K_n}\) is necessary and sufficient for singleton profile resolution. Identify which score approximation, optimized-risk, denominator-ratio, or Gaussian-coupling component first forces nonvanishing undercoverage, while preserving the prescribed curvature, Voronoi margin, and nuisance-rate bounds.
statements.justification: A maximal frontier requires a multi-coordinate undercoverage or ambiguity construction beyond the coordinatewise Le Cam bound.
statements.gap: Levrard2015 and CaiLow2004 provide fixed-loss and adaptive-confidence lower-bound machinery, but neither supplies a geometry-preserving causal experiment for a growing adjacent profile.
statements.consumer: A matching converse would certify the finest resolution any MineThatData analysis can report honestly, irrespective of its estimator or bootstrap implementation.

sampling_model.design: Triangular independent superpopulation sampling under observational assignment or a randomized trial.
sampling_model.units: For each row \(n\), \(O_{n,1},\ldots,O_{n,n}\) are independent and identically distributed from the population law \(P^{(n)}\); \(P_{\mathrm{emp},n}\) is their empirical measure.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment satisfies rowwise consistency and conditional exchangeability.
sampling_model.overlap: The same fixed \(\epsilon\) bounds \(e_{P^{(n)}}(X)\) away from zero and one over the triangular class.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Cross-fitting estimates \(e_{P^{(n)}}\) and \(\mu_{a,P^{(n)}}\) at the common rowwise rate \(r_n\). On every training fold, the fitted propensity is clipped by construction to \(\widehat e^{\mathrm{cl}}(x)=\min\{1-\epsilon/2,\max(\epsilon/2,\widehat e(x))\}\); under overlap this preserves its \(L_2(P_X^{(n)})\) rate, and the clipped fit is used in every corrected loss, estimated influence score, variance estimate, and multiplier-bootstrap coordinate.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: In arXiv:2405.03083v5, Section 4.1, equation (10), and Lemma 4.1 give the fixed-\(k\) optimal-risk influence function; Section 4.2, Assumptions A4--A6, and Lemma 4.2 give fixed-codebook corrected-risk root-\(n\) normality; Remark 3.1 states that \(k\) is fixed and \(k\)-selection or increasing \(k\) is not addressed.

Theorem 3.2 controls pruning and misclassification error for plug-in hierarchical causal clustering under a good-neighborhood condition, and Theorem 4.1 controls Hausdorff error of a smoothed-density level set for the vector counterfactual feature.
Its orthogonal-score multiplier method yields simultaneous bands for many supplied functional parameters under a uniform Bahadur expansion.
Its margin condition gives fixed-level fast excess-distortion bounds and a fixed-level minimax lower bound.
Its positive-Hessian argument gives asymptotic normality of a unique fixed-\(k\) empirical codebook.
Its rectangle approximation covers high-dimensional standardized sums with nondegenerate coordinate variances.
Its generalized moment-selection confidence sets have uniformly correct asymptotic size for supplied moment inequalities.

tldr: For scalar squared-error causal \(k\)-means, the adjacent resolution profile is estimated over a triangular sequence of population laws \(P^{(n)}\), separately from the empirical measure \(P_{\mathrm{emp},n}\). The exact uniform-law score variance has a noise--geometry transition from order \(K^{-4}\) to order \(\nu_n^2K^{-2}\). A corrected optimized-risk expansion through \(K_n\), an adjacent ratio remainder with explicit \(W_{P^{(n)}}(1)\) factors, and a studentized multiplier band yield a uniform sufficient frontier and a locally honest unresolved profile. A polynomial corollary gives an explicit \(K_n\) ceiling, while a score-aligned exponential-tilt causal subfamily proves only coordinatewise standardized-separation necessity and leaves both the full \(\Gamma_n\) boundary and the simultaneous \(\sqrt{\log K_n}\) penalty open. Hierarchical and density-based causal clustering concerns different vector-feature objects and dendrogram or level-set granularities, rather than this adjacent-distortion profile.

project_justification.gap: KimKimKennedy2026 establishes fixed-resolution causal \(k\)-means risk inference, Levrard2015 controls fixed-level quantizer geometry, and BelloniChernozhukovChetverikovWei2018 supplies many-score bands. KimKimWassermanKennedy2024 studies plug-in hierarchical linkages and smoothed-density level sets for a vector counterfactual feature, with pruning, misclassification, and Hausdorff guarantees, but does not define optimized \(k\)-means distortion, normalized distortion profiles, adjacent gains, corrected risk scores, or a growing \(K_n\) frontier. None treats a growing reoptimized scalar squared-error ratio profile under triangular population laws with shrinking adjacent variances.
project_justification.niche: Within scalar squared-error causal \(k\)-means, the exact adjacent variance reveals an observation-noise phase parameter \(\nu_nK\), while the ratio expansion shows that denominator stability and both neighboring optimized risks enter the honest-resolution frontier. This niche is distinct from dendrogram levels and density level sets.
project_justification.fill: The project derives a \(K\)-uniform corrected-risk expansion through \(K_n\), a studentized multiplier band, a locally honest unresolved profile, a transparent polynomial ceiling, an exact uniform-law phase diagram, and a concrete coordinatewise adjacent-resolution lower bound without claiming a generic causal-clustering theorem.

related_work: KimKimKennedy2026 is anchored by the corroborating preprint arXiv:2405.03083v5: Section 4.1, equation (10), and Lemma 4.1 give the fixed-\(k\) optimal-risk influence function; Section 4.2, Assumptions A4--A6, and Lemma 4.2 give fixed-codebook corrected-risk root-\(n\) normality; and Remark 3.1 explicitly says that \(k\) is fixed and that \(k\)-selection and increasing \(k\) are not addressed. The version-of-record receipt currently supports only the Abstract, so the numbered technical locators are identified as arXiv-v5 corroboration. Theorem 1 strictly extends this fixed-\(k\) corrected-risk machinery to a triangular \(K_n\to\infty\), simultaneously studentized adjacent ratio profile with reoptimized neighboring codebooks and possibly shrinking variances. For \(K_n=2\), the result is a one-coordinate ratio delta-method specialization built from the fixed-risk scores, not a claim that KimKimKennedy2026 states the normalized ratio theorem. KimKimWassermanKennedy2024 is a non-overlapping causal-clustering comparator: it studies the vector counterfactual feature \(\mu(X)\) through plug-in hierarchical linkages and density level sets; its Theorem 3.2 controls pruning and misclassification error under a good-neighborhood condition, and its Theorem 4.1 controls Hausdorff error of a smoothed-density level set. It does not define optimized \(k\)-means distortion \(W(K)\), the normalized profile \(\rho(K)\), adjacent gains \(G(K)\), corrected risk scores, simultaneous studentized bands, or a growing \(K_n\) frontier. Its multiple granularities are dendrogram levels, not coordinates of the adjacent-distortion profile, and its lack of a \(k\)-means margin condition reflects the different clustering object. Its stated future-work gap on efficient semiparametric estimators further separates its plug-in guarantees from the corrected-score inference developed here. Theorem 1 is not presented as an extension of KimKimWassermanKennedy2024. Pollard1982Central gives fixed-\(k\) codebook normality under uniqueness and positive curvature. Levrard2015 links Voronoi-boundary margins to fixed-level excess risk and supplies a different fixed-loss converse; its tools inform the stability argument and the explicit adjacent causal lower bound does not claim to extend that theorem. BelloniChernozhukovChetverikovWei2018, ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2017HighDimensional, and ChernozhukovChetverikovKoike2021NearlyOptimal inform the standardized multiplier coupling after the optimized-risk expansion is established. AndrewsSoares2010 and ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2019MMI inform local set-valued reporting for binding moments but do not cover moving causal codebooks. LiuPages2020 studies changing source laws for quantization without adjacent causal-score inference. Hillstrom2008 supplies the public randomized e-mail experiment that motivates a noisy, data-dependent resolution ceiling.
technical_internal_limitation: The geometric raw-loss variance is not the causal efficient-score variance. When \(v_{P^{(n)}}(X)\) is bounded away from zero, the residual term in \(\phi_{W,P^{(n)},K}\) contributes order \(K^{-2}\) to the adjacent variance and dominates the order \(K^{-4}\) geometric contribution. The \(K^{-1}\) standardized-gap law is therefore valid only when \(\nu_nK=O(1)\).
honest_scope: The exact uniform-law variance, the corrected attainable band, the polynomial sufficient ceiling, and a coordinatewise adjacent-resolution lower bound are theorem targets for scalar squared-error causal \(k\)-means. The ordered centers, nearest-center maps, Voronoi boundaries, cell radii, distortion Hessians, optimized-risk influence function, and remainder gauges are specific to that object; no generic causal-quantizer or hierarchical-clustering theorem is claimed. KimKimWassermanKennedy2024 studies vector-feature dendrogram and density-level-set targets and is a non-overlapping comparator. Necessity of every component of \(\Gamma_n(P^{(n)})\) and the simultaneous \(\sqrt{\log K_n}\) separation penalty remain open; the lower bound establishes only coordinatewise standardized-separation necessity. For \(K_n=2\), the band theorem is a one-coordinate ratio delta-method specialization built from the fixed-risk score machinery corroborated in KimKimKennedy2026, arXiv:2405.03083v5, Section 4.1, equation (10), and Lemma 4.1, together with the fixed-codebook corrected-risk conditions and normality in Section 4.2, Assumptions A4--A6, and Lemma 4.2; the normalized ratio is not itself a stated theorem there, and Remark 3.1 leaves \(k\)-selection and increasing \(k\) untreated. The noiseless uniform case reduces to \(W_{P^{(n)}}(K)=1/(12K^2)\).
